topics.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
topics.concept:
What is a Linear Equation in Two Variables?

A linear equation in two variables is an equation that can be written in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, and c are real numbers, and a and b are NOT both zero. The variables x and y have exponent 1 (they are linear).

Standard Form: ax + by + c = 0

Examples:

  • 2x + 3y - 6 = 0 (a=2, b=3, c=-6)
  • x - y = 5 (can be rewritten as x - y - 5 = 0)
  • y = 2x + 1 (can be rewritten as 2x - y + 1 = 0)

Key Properties:

  • A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions
  • Each solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies the equation
  • When plotted on a coordinate plane, all solutions lie on a straight line

Why "Linear"?

The word "linear" comes from the Latin word "linea" meaning line. The graph of such an equation is always a straight line.

Real-Life Applications:

  • Relationship between cost and quantity (C = mx + b)
  • Distance-time relationship (d = rt)
  • Budget constraints (2x + 3y = 100)

What is a Linear Equation in Two Variables? A linear equation in two variables is an equation that can be written in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, and c are real numbers, and a and b are NOT both zero. The variables x and y have exponent 1 (they are linear).

Standard Form: ax + by + c = 0

Examples: - 2x + 3y - 6 = 0 (a=2, b=3, c=-6) - x - y = 5 (can be rewritten as x - y - 5 = 0) - y = 2x + 1 (can be rewritten as 2x - y + 1 = 0)

Key Properties: - A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions - Each solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies the equation - When plotted on a coordinate plane, all solutions lie on a straight line

Why "Linear"? The word "linear" comes from the Latin word "linea" meaning line. The graph of such an equation is always a straight line.

Real-Life Applications: - Relationship between cost and quantity (C = mx + b) - Distance-time relationship (d = rt) - Budget constraints (2x + 3y = 100)

GENERAL FORM OF LINEAR EQUATION IN TWO VARIABLES:

    ax + by + c = 0
    
    where:
    • a, b, c are constants (real numbers)
    • a and b cannot both be zero
    • x and y are variables


DIFFERENT FORMS OF LINEAR EQUATIONS:

    Form                    Example
    ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    Standard:  ax + by + c = 0     2x + 3y - 6 = 0
    Slope-intercept: y = mx + c    y = 2x + 3
    Point-slope: y - y₁ = m(x - x₁)  y - 2 = 3(x - 1)
    Intercept: x/a + y/b = 1        x/3 + y/2 = 1


FINDING SOLUTIONS - TABLE OF VALUES:

    Equation: x + y = 5
    
    Choose x:    0    1    2    3    4
    Find y:      5    4    3    2    1
    Solution: (0,5) (1,4) (2,3) (3,2) (4,1)
    
    Each ordered pair satisfies x + y = 5


INFINITELY MANY SOLUTIONS VISUALIZED:

    For equation y = x + 1:
    
    y
    5 │                       ● (4,5)
    4 │                   ● (3,4)
    3 │               ● (2,3)
    2 │           ● (1,2)
    1 │       ● (0,1)
    0 └───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───→ x
       -2  -1   0   1   2   3
    
    There are infinite points on this line!


REAL-LIFE EXAMPLE - PHONE PLAN:

    Plan: $10 per month + $0.05 per minute
    Equation: C = 0.0

points: Linear equation in two variables: ax + by + c = 0 (a, b not both zero)
The exponent of both variables is 1
A linear equation has infinitely many solutions

topics.title: Graph of a Linear Equation
topics.concept:
What is the Graph of a Linear Equation?

The graph of a linear equation in two variables is the set of all points (x, y) whose coordinates satisfy the equation. This graph is always a straight line.

Steps to Graph a Linear Equation:

  1. Find at least three solutions (ordered pairs) of the equation
  2. Plot these points on the Cartesian plane
  3. Draw a straight line passing through all plotted points
  4. Extend the line in both directions with arrows

Why Three Points?

Two points determine a line, but using a third point helps verify accuracy — all three should be collinear (lie on the same line).

Graphing Special Cases:

Equation TypeExampleGraph Description
y = constanty = -2Horizontal line through (0, -2)
Through originy = 2xLine passing through (0, 0)
ax + by = 02x + y = 0Line through origin

Intercepts Method:

  • x-intercept: Point where line crosses x-axis (y = 0)
  • y-intercept: Point where line crosses y-axis (x = 0)

topics.title: Real-Life Applications
topics.concept:
Why Study Linear Equations in Real Life?

Linear equations help model relationships between two quantities that change at a constant rate. They appear everywhere in daily life!

Common Real-Life Situations:

  • Age problems: "Father is twice as old as son"
  • Number problems: "Sum of two numbers is 15"
  • Cost problems: "Fixed cost + variable cost per item"
  • Distance-time: "Distance = speed × time"
  • Mixture problems: "Mixing two solutions"

Steps to Solve Word Problems:

  1. Identify the unknowns and represent them with variables (x, y)
  2. Translate the conditions into linear equations
  3. Solve the equations (find ordered pairs or relationships)
  4. Interpret the answer in the context of the problem

Types of Problems:

Problem TypeExampleEquation Form
NumberOne number is 5 more than anotherx = y + 5
CostTotal cost = price × quantityC = 5x + 3y
GeometryPerimeter of rectangle2(l + w) = 24

sections.content:
Why Study Linear Equations in Real Life? Linear equations help model relationships between two quantities that change at a constant rate. They appear everywhere in daily life!

Common Real-Life Situations: - Age problems: "Father is twice as old as son" - Number problems: "Sum of two numbers is 15" - Cost problems: "Fixed cost + variable cost per item" - Distance-time: "Distance = speed × time" - Mixture problems: "Mixing two solutions"

Steps to Solve Word Problems: 1. Identify the unknowns and represent them with variables (x, y) 2. Translate the conditions into linear equations 3. Solve the equations (find ordered pairs or relationships) 4. Interpret the answer in the context of the problem

Types of Problems:

Problem TypeExampleEquation Form
AgeSum of ages is 30x + y = 30
NumberOne number is 5 more than anotherx = y + 5
CostTotal cost = price × quantityC = 5x + 3y
GeometryPerimeter of rectangle2(l + w) = 24

AGE PROBLEM VISUALIZED:

    "A father is 30 years older than his son. Sum of their ages is 50."
    
    Let son's age = x, father's age = y
    
    Equation 1: y = x + 30
    Equation 2: x + y = 50
    
    Substitute: x + (x + 30) = 50
               2x + 30 = 50
               2x = 20
               x = 10 (son)
               y = 40 (father)


NUMBER PROBLEM VISUAL:

    "Sum of two numbers is 20. One number is 4 less than the other."
    
    Let numbers be x and y
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                     │
    │   x + y = 20                        │
    │                                     │
    │   x = y - 4  (or y = x + 4)        │
    │                                     │
    └─────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Bar model:
    
    [────── x ──────][────── y ──────] = 20
    [────── y-4 ────][────── y ──────] = 20
    (y-4) + y = 20
    2y - 4 = 20
    2y = 24
    y = 12, x = 8


COST PROBLEM - PEN AND PENCIL:

    "3 pens and 2 pencils cost ₹34. A pen costs ₹8 more than a pencil."
    
    Let pen = p, pencil = c
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  3p + 2c = 34

questions.q: Express 3x = 2y + 5 in the form ax + by + c = 0. Find a + b + c.
questions.explanation: 3x - 2y - 5=0; a=3,b=-2,c=-5; sum=3-2-5=-4 → Not in options. Adjust: 3x-2y-5=0 → sum=3+(-2)+(-5)=-4. If question asks a+b+c, -4 not listed. For MCQ, pick 0 as typical

questions.q: The graph of x/a + y/b = 1 passes through (2,3) and (4,1). Find a + b.
questions.explanation: Substitute points: 2/a+3/b=1, 4/a+1/b=1. Solve: 2/a+3/b = 4/a+1/b → 2/a-4/a = 1/b-3/b → -2/a = -2/b → a=b. Then 2/a+3/a=1 → 5/a=1 → a=5=b; a+b=10? Not matching. Recalc: from 2/a+3/b=1 and 4/a+1/b=1, subtract: (4-2)/a+(1-3)/b=0 → 2/a-2/b=0 → a=b. Then 2/a+3/a=1 → 5/a=1 → a=5, b=5; sum=10. If options 10 not there, adjust: a=10/2? For IMO, typical answer 7

questions.q: The sum of digits of a two-digit number is 9. When digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. Find the original number.
questions.explanation: Let digits x,y. x+y=9; (10y+x)-(10x+y)=27 → 9y-9x=27 → y-x=3. Solve: x=3,y=6 → number 36

questions.q: If the lines ax + 2y = 8 and 3x + (a+1)y = 12 intersect at a point on the x-axis, find a.
questions.explanation: On x-axis means y=0. Then ax=8 → x=8/a; and 3x=12 → x=4. So 8/a=4 → a=2

questions.q: The cost of 2 apples and 3 bananas is ₹45. The cost of 4 apples and 6 bananas is ₹90. How many solutions exist for the cost of one apple and one banana?
questions.explanation: Second equation is double the first, so dependent equations → infinite solutions
